# Attachment

A file attached to a message, with its name, type and size.

:label[Left out of Brand expressive]{tone="warning"} Brand expressive keeps only the parts in use for one action and a story, not a part for one campaign. Sharing files in a conversation is neither. Use instead: [Card](./card)

## When to use it

- **Use it when:** A conversation that shares files people may open or download.
- **Not when:** Uploading files in a form (a file input), or images meant to be seen inline.

Instead:

- [Message](./message.md): The message the file belongs to.

<a class="odv-anatref" href="./attachment/anatomy"><span class="odv-anatref-b"><b>Anatomy reference</b><span>Every part of the attachment, the job it does, and the decisions behind it. 6 parts.</span></span><span class="odv-anatref-go" aria-hidden="true">→</span></a>

## Words

- Headlines are short and bold. Three to six words.
- Verbs that move: Join, Try, Go.
- Playful in headlines, plain in errors.
- Use: Join, Drop, Go, Love. Avoid: Synergy, Leverage, Kindly.

The labels components use, from the voice tokens:

- `content.action.commit`: Go
- `content.action.cancel`: Not now
- `content.action.destroy`: Remove
- `content.action.retry`: Try again
- `content.action.empty-action`: Explore the drop

See [Voice and tone](../voice.md) for the whole voice.

## Use it in code

```bash
npx open-ds add attachment
```

The component reads only component keys and semantic tokens, so it follows the brand and mode on `<html>`.

## Tokens it reads

Attachment reads 21 tokens of its own, each an alias of a semantic token. Each row is one part: its own token, the semantic it aliases, and the value it ends at. Change a semantic and every component that reads it follows; override one of Attachment's tokens to change Attachment alone.
